say: The tracker is fixed. Here is what changed.
Blocks would not save. You would type the whole thing, press send, and get an error. That is gone.
Signing in took up to thirty seconds. It now takes about one.
cap:
Signing in takes
about a second.

say: Your typing is saved as you type. Close the page. Lose signal. Come back. What you wrote is still there.
If a send fails it tries again on its own. You will see it counting.
One thing is new. If a block reads thin, it asks once.
A name on its own. A number attached to nothing. Three words.
Three tasks. Which three. For whom. And what came of them. That is the whole difference.
cap:
Which three.
For whom.
What came of them.

say: It asks what was done. Then it sends whatever you write. It is a prompt, not a gate.
This is what a block looks like when it is right.
cap:
What was done.
What came of it.

say: Salesforce shows that a task moved. It does not show the work.
cap:
Salesforce shows a task moved.
It does not show the work.

say: So your block and Salesforce have to agree. If your block says three closed, Salesforce should show three.
cap:
Your block and Salesforce
have to agree.
sub:
If the block says three closed,
Salesforce should show three.

say: Moving a task forward with nothing written on it leaves no record that anything was done.
cap:
A task moved with nothing
written on it is not
a record of work.

say: A line in the description, or a note in the chatter feed. Either one counts. Neither one is optional.
sub: One of the two, on every task you touch.

say: Your block is the record. It is what the branch reports. It is what stands behind your name.
sub:
It is what the branch reports.
It is what stands behind your name.

say: This is part of the job, not extra to it.
cap:
Part of the job.
Not extra to it.

say: Four blocks. Two minutes each. Written while you still remember it.
